title: What If the Dust Bowl Happened Again?

scenes.text: What if the Dust Bowl happened again? In 1935, one storm was a thousand miles long.
Black Sunday hit on April 14, 1935. Temperatures fell more than 30 degrees in hours as the dust wall arrived.
Estimates say about 300,000 tons of topsoil blew away that day, and some of it reached the East Coast.
The drought ran from 1931 through the decade, and 1934 was the worst drought year in the last thousand years.
Dust killed hundreds and sickened thousands. Up to a third of the hardest-hit residents left the Southern Plains.
Contour plowing and crop rotation have since cut soil loss by about 65 percent. A repeat would look different.
